html.body: Date: 2025-03-24 REMARKSBy this amendment, claims 195, 199-207, and 210-212 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer. Claims 193, 194, 196-198, 208, and 209 are amended. New claims 213-232 are added.As a result, claims 193, 194, 196-198, 208, 209, and 213-232 are pending for examination with claims 193 and 208 being independent claims. No new matter has been added.Allowable Subject Matter The Office Action indicates that claim 196 would be allowable if rewritten to overcome the double patenting rejection and the rejection(s) under 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, set forth in this Office action and to include all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.The identification of this allowable subject matter is gratefully acknowledged.Double Patenting Rejections Claims 193-212 are rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as being unpatentable over claims 1, 2, 3, 7, 9, 13, 15, and 22-23 of U.S. Patent No. 8,808,202.This rejection will be addressed if it is the only remaining rejection of the claims.Rejections under 35 U.S.C. §112 Claims 193-212 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. §112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite.Claim 193 is rejected for reciting the language "at least when". Without acceding to the propriety of this rejection, this language is cancelled from the claim without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 208 is rejected for lacking antecedent basis for "the skin". Claim 208 is amended to recite "the subject's skin." Without acceding to the propriety of the rejections, claims 200, 202 and 207 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections of claims 193, 194, 196-198 and 208-210 is respectfully requested.Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. §102 Independent claim 208 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §102(b) as being anticipated by U.S. Patent No. 6,027,459 to Shain (hereinafter, "Shain").In addition to other features, independent claim 208 is amended to recite that the device comprises a flexible concave member and a spring, where actuating the device actuator causes the flexible concave member to move from a first configuration to a second configuration, and causes compression of the spring. Shain does not teach or suggest all of the features of claim 208.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections of independent claim 208 and its corresponding dependent claims is respectfully requested.Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. § 103 Claims 193-195 and 197-200 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over U.S. Patent No. 6,024,710 to Miller (hereinafter, "Miller") in view of U.S. Publication No. 2007/0213638 to Herbrechtsmeier et al. (hereinafter, "Herbrechtsmeier").Independent claim 193 recites a flexible concave member, wherein the flexible concave member is moveable from a first configuration to a second configuration in response to actuation of the device actuator. In addition to other features, claim 193 is amended to recite a spring positioned such that actuation of the device actuator causes compression of the spring. Neither Miller nor Herbrechtsmeier teach or suggest all the features of amended claim 193.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejection of claim 193 and its corresponding dependent claims 194, 197 and 198 is respectfully requested.Claims 195, 199 and 200 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Rejections of dependent claims Claim 201 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Miller in view of Herbrechtsmeier as applied to claim 193 above in further view of U.S. Publication No.2008/0125673 to Carano et al. (hereinafter, "Carano").Claim 201 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claims 202 and 204-205 are rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Miller in view of U.S. Publication No. 2009/0299224 to Yoo (hereinafter, "Yoo").Claims 202 and 204-205 are cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 203 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Miller in view of Yoo as applied to claim 202 above in further view of Herbrechtsmeier.Claim 203 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 206 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Miller in view of Yoo as applied to claim 202 above in further view of Carano.Claim 206 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 209 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over US Patent No.6027 459 to Shain et al. (hereinafter, "Shain") as applied to claim 208 above in further view of Herbrechtsmeier.Claim 209 depends from claim 208 and is allowable for at least the reasons that claim 208 is allowable.Claim 210 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Shain applied to claim 208 above in further view of Miller.Claim 210 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 211 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Shain.Claim 211 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Claim 212 is rejected under pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. §103(a) as being obvious over Shain as applied to claim 208 above in further view of Carano.Claim 212 is cancelled without prejudice or disclaimer.Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections of independent claims 193 and 202 and its corresponding dependent claims is respectfully requested.General Comments on Dependent Claims Since each of the dependent claims depends from a base claim that is believed to be in condition for allowance, for the sake of brevity, Applicant believes that it is unnecessary at this time to argue the further distinguishing features of the dependent claims. However, Applicant does not necessarily concur with the interpretation of the previously presented dependent claims as set forth in the Office Action, nor does Applicant concur that the basis for rejection of any of the previously presented dependent claims is proper. Therefore, Applicant reserves the right to specifically address the further patentability of the dependent claims in the future.CONCLUSIONIn view of the foregoing, this application should now be in condition for allowance. A notice to this effect is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes, after this response, the application is not in condition for allowance, the Examiner is requested to call the undersigned at the telephone number indicated below to discuss any outstanding issues.If this response is not considered timely filed and if a request for an extension of time is otherwise absent, Applicant hereby requests any necessary extension of time.Applicant believes no fee is due with this Amendment. However, if a fee is due with this Amendment, please charge our Deposit Account No. 23/2825, under Docket No. L0693.70035US04 from which the undersigned is authorized to draw.Dated: March 24, 2025 Respectfully submitted, By /Jennifer J. Wang/ Jennifer J. Wang Registration No.: 68,598 WOLF, GREENFIELD & SACKS, P.C.600 Atlantic Avenue Boston, Massachusetts 02210-2206 617.646.8000
